data.text/markdown:
Prediction intervals: parametric vs conformal

statsforecast offers two routes to an 80% band:
  • Parametric (SeasonalNaive, HistoricAverage, AutoETS, AutoARIMA): derived from the model's own error assumptions (Gaussian, constant variance, variance growing with horizon).
  • Conformal (ConformalIntervals(h=48, n_windows=3), any model): residuals from past rolling forecasts set the band width. No distributional assumption, but it needs n_windows * h extra history. Some models (MSTL, SeasonalWindowAverage) have only this option.
Question: which is better calibrated (coverage near 80%) for this half-hourly data, and at what width?

data.text/markdown:
Takeaways to check against the table

  1. Parametric bands assume Gaussian, homoscedastic errors. Net load with solar breaks both, so expect under- or over-coverage depending on the hour.
  2. Conformal fixes average coverage but not shape.
  3. For hour-varying bands you need per-slot conformal scores or quantile models (see mlforecast).
